[SPEC] Issuer key status : RESERVED / ACTIVE / DEPRECATED / REVOKED
RESERVED = key placed in the DID at creation , not used for signing yet
Only one ACTIVE key per identity (unique index on IdentityId + Status = ACTIVE)
No ACTIVE key → handled in section 5.2 (switch to the next RESERVED key)
More than one ACTIVE key → configuration error , do not guess

[SPEC] Final 1.0 has a separate nonce endpoint
Only Final 1.0 is installed , so there is no choice to make here
Nonce is fetched once and used for every proof in the same batch
Load holder private key (created at wallet activation)
Build proof JWT and sign with on-device key
jwk = holder public key , aud = credential_issuer (from offer) , nonce = c_nonce , iat
[ENGINE RULE] proof header must contain exactly one of kid or jwk
We use jwk because the holder has no DID , a kid starting with did: makes the engine resolve the DID instead
iss must be omitted because a pre-authorized code is used (OpenID4VCI)
With key attestation the header must be kid = index of the key in the attestation + key_attestation , without jwk
the engine then takes the holder public key from the attestation
Normally one signature , with batch enabled one proof per key , all sent together

Build SD_JWT_VC and compute _sd digests of selectively disclosable claims
Sign SD-JWT (JWS) with issuer signing key (ECDSA / ES256)
Issuer signature (private key never leaves HSM)
kid = verificationMethod id of the issuer did:web , format did:web:...#key-{keyId}
payload : vct , vct#integrity , iss = issuer did:web
iat , nbf , status.status_list = { uri , idx } (Token Status List)
cnf.jwk = holder public key , raw EC P-256
Disclosures appended with ~ , each is [ salt , technicalKey , value ]
sub is present only when the holder uses a DID identifier
With a KEY identifier , as chosen , there is no sub and no holder DID anywhere in the credential
exp is present only when credential validity is configured , otherwise only iat and nbf
[SIGNING POINT 2] Required setup , otherwise signing fails
1. The issuing key must be declared in the DID Document under assertionMethod
the engine looks up kid in this relationship , signing fails if not found
2. The vct URL must be resolvable , by default the engine hosts it at /ssi/vct/v2/{orgId}/{schemaId}/SD_JWT_VC
if moved to our domain it must still resolve
3. The Token Status List must be published and resolvable at /ssi/revocation/v1/list/{id}
the list is a JWT signed with the same issuer key
[AUDIT LOG] Write audit record of /ssi credential (eventType = CREDENTIAL_ISSUED , EngineCalls)
holder key reference + cnf thumbprint (not a DID)
number of proofs received in the request (batch)
no personal data claims in the audit trail
Read iss and kid from the credential (→ issuer DID document)
Read vct from the credential (→ vct type metadata)
[SPEC] Goal : the app checks the credential is genuine and usable before saving it
Check 1 : the issuer really signed it and nothing was changed (see the note under Verify issuer signature)
Check 2 : the issuer is trusted (issuer DID (iss) is listed in the Trust Registry and its accreditation has not expired)
Check 3 : the credential is bound to this phone (holder key in the credential (cnf.jwk) = the key on this device)
Check 4 : the credential type is the one offered and its description was not changed (vct , vct#integrity)
Any check fails : tell the engine (credential_failure) and DW (issuance_result FAILED) , the card/document is not added
All checks pass : save the credential (9.1 , 9.2) , tell the engine (credential_accepted) and DW (issuance_result ACCEPTED) (9.3)
[NEW] Get issuer DID document from iss (did:web) | GET /ssi/did-web/v1/{id}/did.json
using the public key of the verificationMethod matching kid
[SPEC] Goal : prove the credential was signed by the issuer and was not changed
Required by RFC 9901 (SD-JWT) section 7.2 , done on the app because only the app receives the full credential
Step 1 : read from the credential the signing key id (kid) and the issuer (iss)
Step 2 : check the key belongs to the issuer (the DID before # in kid = iss)
Step 3 : in the issuer DID document (request above) , find the public key whose id = kid
Step 4 : check that key is allowed to sign credentials (kid is listed in assertionMethod)
Step 5 : give the credential and that public key to an SD-JWT library , it checks the signature and every disclosure
With the Procivis wallet SDK , steps 1 to 5 run inside issuance-accept
Any step fails → Verification failed branch below
[NEW] Check issuer DID (iss) is listed and accreditation not expired (Check 2) | GET {trust registry URL}
Check cnf.jwk matches the public key of the key on this device (Check 3)
[SPEC] Why the holder key is checked now (Check 3)
The credential works only with the key whose public key is in cnf.jwk
If that is not the key on this device , the user can never present this credential to a verifier
(the app cannot create the key binding proof (Key Binding JWT) that the verifier requires)
Check it here before saving , not later when the user presents the credential

Get credential type description (vct type metadata) | GET /ssi/vct/v2/{orgId}/{credentialSchemaId}/SD_JWT_VC (endpoint 25)

hash of the credential type description just downloaded = vct#integrity in the credential

9.1 Credential Storage Model (on device or cloud)
[PENDING] Two storage modes are kept in the design , one will be removed later
In both modes the holder private key stays on the device
[DATA STORE] Store the full token (SD_JWT_VC + disclosures) in the on-device database
[DATA STORE] Store credential metadata in on-device database
Bind credentialId to holder key reference
Mark credential as available for presentation
The wallet owns the full token , so it can present offline
and does not disclose data to backend systems when presenting a VP
Holder private key remains on device
Backend does not keep the full VC , only references
[Storage mode = CLOUD (encrypted on the device before upload)]
Encrypt the full token (SD_JWT_VC + disclosures) on the device
with a data key protected by secure hardware (Secure Enclave / Android Keystore)
[NEW] Store encrypted credential + Token | POST /dw/v1/credentials (DW endpoint 08)
[DATA STORE] Store encrypted credential in DW cloud storage
credential metadata : credentialType , vct , issuer DID , validFrom / validUntil , status reference ( uri + idx )
[DATA STORE] Store credential metadata + cloud reference in on-device database
Bind credentialId to holder key reference
Mark credential as available for presentation
The token is encrypted on the device , DW stores only ciphertext and metadata
To present a VP the app downloads the ciphertext , decrypts it on the device and signs with the on-device key
Holder private key remains on device
[PENDING] Recovery of the data key when the device is lost or replaced
Whether credential metadata on DW may be stored in clear
Endpoint name POST /dw/v1/credentials (DW endpoint 08) is a placeholder
9.2 Secure Local Storage and Access Policy
[SPEC] Applies to the on-device database in both modes
In CLOUD mode it holds credential metadata and the cloud reference , not the full token
Use secure local storage for the on-device database (from 9.1)
Encrypt the database with envelope encryption
KEK in secure hardware protects DEK on disk , DEK encrypts the data files
Set file protection so data is unreadable while the screen is locked
not only until first unlock after boot
Protect credential access with device security
Store only the personal data that is necessary
do not keep readable claim copies without justification
Prevent export of holder private key
require holder signing before VP submission
[SPEC] Target is OWASP MASVS-STORAGE level L2
The library provides only L1 , the gap must be implemented
